Polish Media & Publishing Workers Strike Halts Newsrooms, Delays Publications

A nationwide strike by workers in Poland’s Media & Publishing industry entered its second day Wednesday, disrupting editorial operations and delaying major print and digital publications across the country. Staff at leading media houses, including Gazeta Polska Media Group, Wydawnictwo Nowa Era, and Słowo24, walked out in protest over stalled wage negotiations and working conditions.

Newsrooms in Warsaw, Kraków, and Gdańsk have reported sharply reduced staffing, forcing the suspension of several print editions and limiting the frequency of online updates. “With a majority of our editorial and production staff on strike, we’ve had no choice but to delay the morning and evening editions,” said Elżbieta Kurek, spokesperson for Wydawnictwo Nowa Era. “We are urging all parties to return to the negotiating table.”

The Media Workers’ Union, which represents over 6,000 journalists, editors, and production staff, said more than 80% of its members are participating in the walkout. “Our members are committed to quality journalism, but they deserve fair pay and reasonable hours,” said union president Tomasz Zawistowski. He said the strike would continue until management offers “meaningful improvements.”

Industry analysts estimate that at least 75% of regular newsprint output is currently suspended, with most daily newspapers publishing only skeletal digital editions. Several leading news sites, including Dziennik Polska24 and Fakt24, have posted notices warning of limited coverage or temporarily suspended updates.

“This disruption highlights the vital role skilled staff play in producing reliable news and publications,” said Agata Nowicka, an independent media analyst based in Łódź. “Prolonged action could impact the industry’s revenue streams and erode reader trust.”

Negotiations between union representatives and company management are scheduled to resume later this week. Industry observers say a swift resolution is needed to restore normal publishing operations.
